questions.question: How much blood is in a typical adult's body?
questions.fact: Men and women carry about the same share of their body weight as blood, 7 to 8%.

questions.question: How many bones are in an adult human skeleton?
questions.fact: Babies are born with around 270; some of them fuse together on the way to adulthood.

questions.question: How tall was Robert Wadlow, the tallest person ever recorded?
questions.fact: He weighed 199 kg when he died, aged 22.

questions.question: How long does an African bush elephant's pregnancy last?
questions.fact: It's the longest pregnancy of any mammal.

questions.question: How tall is the Eiffel Tower?
questions.fact: It was the tallest human-made structure in the world for 41 years, until New York's Chrysler Building was finished.

questions.question: What is the population of New York City?
questions.fact: An estimated 800 languages are spoken there, making it the most linguistically diverse city in the world.

questions.question: How long does the International Space Station take to circle Earth once?
questions.fact: That's 15.5 laps a day, so its crew sees 16 sunrises and sunsets every day.

questions.question: How many people walked on the Moon during the Apollo program?
questions.fact: Six Apollo landings each set two astronauts down on the surface while a third waited in orbit.

questions.question: How hot must the oven be for a true Neapolitan pizza?
questions.fact: At that heat the pizza bakes in 60 to 90 seconds.

questions.question: How many passengers can an Airbus A380, the biggest airliner, carry?
questions.fact: In the evacuation test, everyone got out in 78 seconds with half the exits blocked.

questions.question: How much water does an Olympic swimming pool hold?
questions.fact: It's 50 m long, 25 m wide and at least 2 m deep: 2,500 cubic metres of water.

questions.question: How far is a marathon?
questions.fact: The distance was fixed in 1921, copied from the course of the 1908 London Olympics.

questions.question: How long did the longest professional tennis match last?
questions.fact: John Isner beat Nicolas Mahut 70-68 in the fifth set, after 11 hours 5 minutes spread over three days.

source.title: Isner–Mahut match at the 2010 Wimbledon Championships

questions.question: How many keys does a modern piano have?
questions.fact: In Mozart's day pianos had five octaves; today's 88 keys span more than seven.

questions.question: How much beer do Czechs, the world's top beer drinkers, get through a year?
questions.fact: That's about 250 half-litre glasses for every Czech, children included, and no country drinks more.

source.title: List of countries by beer consumption per capita

questions.question: How long is the record for holding your breath?
questions.definition: official freediving record, breathing only air first
questions.fact: Breathe pure oxygen beforehand and the record is over 29 minutes.

questions.question: How much does an ostrich egg weigh?
questions.fact: That is over 20 times a chicken's egg, yet it's the smallest egg of any bird relative to the mother's size.

questions.question: How fast can a hummingbird's heart beat?
questions.definition: fastest measured, in a blue-throated hummingbird
questions.fact: At night, in a torpor, a hummingbird's heart can slow to around 50 beats a minute.

questions.question: How fast can a cheetah run?
questions.fact: Its acceleration is the real weapon: from 0 to 97 km/h in under 3 seconds.

questions.question: How many people live in Antarctica in winter?
questions.fact: In summer the number swells to about four times that.

questions.question: How many hot dogs did the record holder eat in 10 minutes?
questions.fact: Takeru Kobayashi once ate 50, nearly doubling the old record of 25.5.

questions.question: How fast does Earth spin at the equator?
questions.fact: It slows away from the equator: about 1,184 km/h at 45° latitude, and zero at the poles.

questions.question: How fast did Usain Bolt run at his top speed?
questions.definition: during his 100 m world record, 9.58 s
questions.fact: His average over the whole race, start included, was 37.58 km/h.

questions.question: How high is the men's high jump world record?
questions.fact: Javier Sotomayor set it in 1993, and nobody has beaten it since.

source.title: Men's high jump world record progression

questions.question: How much of the Moon's surface can we see from Earth?
questions.fact: It always turns the same face to us, but it wobbles as it orbits, so we see a little way round its edges.

questions.question: In what year did the Wright brothers first fly a plane?
questions.fact: That first flight, at Kitty Hawk in North Carolina, lasted 12 seconds and covered 37 metres.

questions.question: In what year was the first video uploaded to YouTube?
questions.fact: Called Me at the Zoo, it is 19 seconds of co-founder Jawed Karim in front of the elephants at San Diego Zoo.

questions.question: How much does a fingernail grow in a month?
questions.fact: Toenails grow about half as fast, about 1.6 mm a month, and a whole fingernail takes three to six months to regrow.

questions.question: How old was the oldest person whose age has been verified?
questions.fact: Jeanne Calment of France lived 122 years and 164 days, and said that at 13 she had met Vincent van Gogh in her uncle's shop.

questions.question: How long is a day on the Moon, from one sunrise to the next?
questions.fact: It matches the cycle of the Moon's phases, because the Moon turns once per orbit and always shows us the same face.

questions.question: How long did NASA's Perseverance rover take to fly from Earth to Mars?
questions.fact: It left in a launch window of under a month, when Earth and Mars were best placed for the trip, alongside missions from China and the UAE.

questions.question: How long is the longest single trip anyone has made in space?
questions.fact: Valeri Polyakov spent it on the Mir space station, to learn how a human body would cope with a long trip to Mars.

questions.question: How many eggs can a laying hen produce in a year?
questions.fact: The record is 371 eggs in 364 days.

questions.question: How much food can an elephant eat in a day?
questions.fact: Less than half of it gets digested, so its dung feeds other animals, from dung beetles to monkeys.

questions.question: How old are the oldest known remains of bread?
questions.fact: It was found at a Natufian site in Jordan's north-eastern desert, and is thousands of years older than farming.

questions.question: How much did one US penny, the 1-cent coin, cost to make?
questions.fact: Losing money on every coin is largely why the Mint stopped making pennies for circulation in November 2025.

questions.question: How fast did Concorde, the supersonic passenger jet, fly?
questions.fact: That's more than twice the speed of other airliners, so it crossed the Atlantic in just under 3.5 hours.

questions.question: How long is a football pitch?
questions.definition: FIFA's recommended size for top matches
questions.fact: The Laws of the Game allow anything from 91 to 119 m, so pitches really do vary.

questions.question: How far does a rider cycle in the Tour de France, the three-week race?
questions.fact: It's split into 21 stages over three weeks, with only two rest days.

questions.question: How long did the fastest Formula One pit stop take?
questions.fact: A crew of up to 20 mechanics changes all four tyres in that time.

questions.question: How much did PSG pay Barcelona for Neymar?
questions.definition: the record transfer fee, not wages
questions.fact: It more than doubled the previous record, Paul Pogba's move to Manchester United a year earlier.

source.title: List of most expensive association football transfers

questions.question: How many people have ever been born?
questions.fact: That makes the people alive today about 6.7% of everyone who has ever lived.

questions.question: How long ago did our species, Homo sapiens, first appear?
questions.fact: For all but the last 12,000 or so of those years, every human lived as a hunter-gatherer.

questions.question: How far away is the horizon when you look out to sea?
questions.definition: standing on the beach, eyes 1.7 m up
questions.fact: Climb a 100 m tower and it's 35.7 km away.

questions.question: How fast does a skydiver fall before the parachute opens?
questions.fact: Jumping from 38,887 m up, where the air is thin, Felix Baumgartner reached 380 m/s, about 1,368 km/h.

questions.question: How many oil paintings did Vincent van Gogh make?
questions.fact: With drawings and watercolours he made about 2,100 works, most of them in the last two years of his life.
questions.definition: in a career of just over ten years

questions.question: How much did the most expensive painting ever sold go for?
questions.fact: Decades earlier it had sold for just £45, when it was thought to be the work of a follower.

questions.question: How many people watched the first Moon landing live on TV?
questions.fact: That was roughly one in five of everyone alive at the time.

questions.question: How long did it take to build the Empire State Building?
questions.definition: first steel columns to opening day
questions.fact: At its fastest the frame rose by about four and a half floors a week.

questions.question: How deep is the deepest hole ever drilled?
questions.fact: It took 19 years to drill, and got only about a third of the way through the crust beneath it.

questions.question: How much did the first handheld mobile phone weigh?
questions.definition: Motorola DynaTAC, the version approved for sale
questions.fact: A full charge took about 10 hours and gave just 30 minutes of talking.

questions.question: How many heartbeats does a person have in a lifetime?
questions.fact: A resting adult heart beats 60 to 100 times a minute, so even a slow one tops 86,000 beats a day.

questions.question: How much blood does the heart pump in a day?
questions.fact: At rest it pushes out about 70 ml with each beat, some 70 times a minute.

questions.question: How many teeth does an adult have?
questions.definition: a full set, wisdom teeth included
questions.fact: Children have 20 baby teeth, and the wisdom teeth at the back usually come through between 17 and 25.

questions.question: How many times a minute does a person blink?
questions.fact: Reading or staring at one thing slows it to about 4 or 5 a minute.

questions.question: Spending a dollar a second, how long would a billion dollars last?
questions.fact: At the same rate a million dollars would be gone in under 12 days.

questions.question: How many matches were played at the 2026 World Cup?
questions.definition: 48 teams, in groups of four, then knockouts
questions.fact: Twelve groups of four played six matches each, and the knockout rounds from the last 32 added 32 more.

questions.question: How many spaces are there around a Monopoly board?
questions.fact: Twenty-eight of them are properties to buy: 22 streets, four railroads and two utilities.

questions.question: How many panels make up a classic black-and-white football?
questions.fact: Twelve are pentagons and twenty are hexagons, the pattern that made the ball a symbol of the game.

questions.question: How many smartphones were shipped worldwide in 2019?
questions.fact: Shipments first topped a billion a year in 2013, when smartphones passed half of all mobile phones sold.

questions.question: How many cars are there in the world?
questions.fact: Between them they burn over a trillion litres of petrol and diesel a year.

questions.question: How many calories are in a Big Mac?
questions.fact: Over half of them, 306, come from its fat.

questions.question: How much pasta does an Italian eat in a year?
questions.definition: per person, by weight as sold, 2015
questions.fact: That's the most of any country, ahead of Tunisia at 16 kg a person.

questions.question: How many people live in Vatican City, the smallest country?
questions.fact: They are clergy and other religious, the Swiss Guard and lay staff, and their families.

questions.question: How long ago did the last woolly mammoths die out?
questions.fact: Most had died out at the end of the Ice Age, but a few hung on until then on Wrangel Island, off Siberia.

questions.question: How far is it from the North Pole to the equator?
questions.fact: The metre was first defined as one ten-millionth of this distance, which is why it's so round.

questions.question: How many time zones does Russia span?
questions.fact: It stretches some 9,000 km from west to east, across 172 of the world's 360 degrees of longitude.

questions.question: How many countries are there in Africa?
questions.fact: Most of them kept the borders drawn by colonial powers when they became independent.

questions.question: How many people give a 50% chance two share a birthday?
questions.fact: With 23 people there are 253 pairs, and each pair is a fresh chance of a match.

questions.question: How much sugar is in a can of Coca-Cola?
questions.fact: It gives the can all of its 140 calories, since there is no fat in it.

questions.question: How long is the ball in play during a football match?
questions.fact: Stoppage time doesn't make up for all the time lost to throw-ins, free kicks and goal kicks.

questions.question: How many sheep are there in New Zealand?
questions.fact: It once had 39 million, nearly 10 for every New Zealander, before forests took over farmland.

questions.question: How far does a Formula One car race in a Grand Prix?
questions.fact: Lap lengths vary from track to track, so each race sets its number of laps to make up the distance.

questions.question: How many sheets of A4 paper would cover a square metre?
questions.fact: A0 is exactly one square metre, and each size down is half the one before, so A4 is a sixteenth.

questions.question: How many McDonald's are there in the United States?
questions.fact: Mainland China comes next with over 7,700, then Japan with over 3,000.

source.title: List of countries with McDonald's restaurants

questions.question: How many people speak English?
questions.definition: as a first or second language, 2026
questions.fact: Only about 450 million of them are native speakers.

source.title: List of languages by total number of speakers

questions.question: What share of Earth's water is fresh water?
questions.fact: About 69% of that is frozen as ice and snow, and only 0.3% is liquid water at the surface.

questions.question: What share of Earth's land is covered by forest?
questions.fact: More than half of all forest is in just five countries: Russia, Brazil, Canada, the US and China.

questions.question: What share of the Netherlands lies below sea level?
questions.fact: About 21% of the Dutch live below sea level too, on land kept dry by dykes, canals and pumping stations.

questions.question: What share of the world's people live south of the equator?
questions.fact: It holds only 32.7% of Earth's land, since 80.9% of its surface is water.

questions.question: What share of Earth's mammals, by weight, are wild, not people or farm animals?
questions.fact: On land it's under 2%: nearly all the rest is people and farm animals.

questions.question: What share of the world's people use the internet?
questions.fact: That's up from 60% in 2020, but still leaves about 2.2 billion people offline.

questions.question: What share of all known animal species are beetles?
questions.fact: With hundreds of thousands of described species, beetles are the largest order of all, and almost 40% of known arthropods.

questions.question: On Mars, what share of your Earth weight would you feel?
questions.fact: Mars is about half Earth's width but has only 11% of its mass, so it pulls far less.

questions.question: What share of the Amazon rainforest is in Brazil?
questions.fact: Peru has 13% and Colombia 10%, and six more countries and territories share the rest.

questions.question: What share of Greenland is covered by ice?
questions.fact: If it all melted, the oceans would rise by about 7.4 m.

questions.question: What share of an avocado's flesh is fat?
questions.fact: Most of the rest is water, about 73%.

questions.question: What share of men are red-green colour blind?
questions.fact: In women it's only about 0.5%, because the genes for it sit on the X chromosome.

questions.question: What share of the world's earthquakes hit the Ring of Fire, around the Pacific's edge?
questions.fact: The belt runs about 40,000 km around the Pacific, and holds about two thirds of the world's volcanoes too.

questions.question: What share of people are left-handed?
questions.fact: If both parents are left-handed, their child has a 26% chance of being left-handed too.

questions.question: What share of an adult's body weight is water?
questions.fact: Muscle is about 75% water and fat only about 10%, so the share varies from person to person.

questions.question: How much of the London Underground actually runs underground?
questions.fact: Most of the track out in the open is north of the River Thames, on the lines' long outer branches.

questions.question: How much of Earth's surface does the Pacific Ocean cover?
questions.fact: That's more than all of Earth's land put together.

questions.question: How much of the world's coffee does Brazil grow?
questions.fact: Vietnam comes second, and in the 1910s Brazil exported about 70% of all the world's coffee.

questions.question: How much of the world's maple syrup comes from Canada?
questions.fact: Quebec alone makes 90% of Canada's, and nearly all the rest of the world's comes from the United States.

questions.question: What share of penalty kicks are scored?
questions.fact: In World Cup penalty shootouts only 69.4% go in.

questions.question: What share of the world's people live where cars drive on the left?
questions.fact: The 75 countries that drive on the left cover only about a sixth of the world's land.

questions.question: What share of Icelanders live in and around Reykjavík?
questions.fact: The city itself has about 140,000 people, and six towns around it make up the rest.

questions.question: How much of Switzerland do the Alps cover?
questions.fact: Yet most of its 9 million people live on the flatter plateau to the north, around Zurich, Geneva and Basel.

questions.question: What share of Canadians live within 150 km of the US border?
questions.fact: That leaves about a fifth of the people for the rest of the world's second-largest country.

questions.question: How much of an iceberg is under the water?
questions.fact: Ice is only a little lighter than seawater: about 920 kg a cubic metre against 1,025.

questions.question: When did the first iPhone go on sale?
questions.fact: It launched without an App Store, which only opened a year later.

questions.question: When was the first email sent from one computer to another?
questions.fact: Ray Tomlinson sent it over ARPANET, and picked the @ sign to separate the user's name from the computer's.

questions.question: When was the first text message sent to a mobile phone?
questions.fact: It read 'Merry Christmas', and was typed on a personal computer and sent to a colleague's phone.

questions.question: When were the first bitcoins created?
questions.fact: The first notable purchase of goods with them came the next year: two pizzas for ten thousand bitcoins.

questions.question: When did the Titanic sink?
questions.fact: It went down on its maiden voyage, less than three hours after hitting an iceberg.

questions.question: When was the first satellite, Sputnik 1, launched?
questions.fact: It circled Earth every 96 minutes, beeping, until its batteries died three weeks later.

questions.question: When were the first modern Olympic Games held?
questions.fact: They took place in Athens, with 241 athletes from 14 nations, all of them men.

questions.question: When was the first Harry Potter book published?
questions.fact: Most publishers thought it too long, until the eight-year-old daughter of Bloomsbury's boss said it was 'so much better than anything else'.

source.title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone

questions.question: When was the modern Lego brick designed?
questions.fact: Bricks made that year still click together with the ones sold today.

questions.question: When did Alexander Fleming discover penicillin?
questions.fact: He spotted a mould killing the bacteria on a dish he had left out while away on holiday.

questions.question: When did the world's first underground railway open, in London?
questions.fact: Steam engines pulled its trains, filling stations and carriages with smoke, until the line was electrified in 1905.

questions.question: When was Mount Everest first climbed to the top?
questions.fact: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reached the top on 29 May, and the news broke in London on the morning of Queen Elizabeth II's coronation.

questions.question: When was Coca-Cola invented?
questions.fact: John Pemberton first sold it at an Atlanta pharmacy for five cents a glass, as an alcohol-free take on his coca wine tonic.

questions.question: When was the first human heart transplant?
questions.fact: Christiaan Barnard did it in Cape Town, and his patient lived for 18 days.

questions.question: When was Pluto demoted from planet to dwarf planet?
questions.fact: The find of Eris, an icy world beyond Neptune more massive than Pluto, forced astronomers to define a planet.

questions.question: When did euro coins and notes go into circulation?
questions.fact: The euro itself began in 1999, but at first only on screens and in bank accounts.

questions.question: When were the first traffic lights put up?
questions.fact: A police officer raised and lowered their semaphore arms by day and, at night, worked a lever for red and green lights.

questions.question: When was the first football World Cup played?
questions.fact: Uruguay hosted it to mark 100 years of its independence, and won it.

questions.question: When did the world's population reach 4 billion?
questions.fact: It took only 48 years more to double again, to 8 billion in November 2022.

questions.question: When did people first fly, in a hot-air balloon?
questions.fact: Étienne Montgolfier, of a family of French paper makers, went up first, tethered, from a Paris workshop yard.

questions.question: When did Elizabeth II become queen?
questions.fact: She was 25, and reigned for 70 years and 214 days, the longest of any British monarch.

questions.question: When was the World Wide Web released to the whole internet?
questions.fact: Tim Berners-Lee had it running at CERN by the end of 1990; other research labs got it some months before everyone else.

questions.question: When did anyone last walk on the Moon?
questions.fact: It was Apollo 17, and no one flew beyond low Earth orbit again until a Moon flyby in April 2026.

questions.question: When was the first selfie taken?
questions.definition: a photo of yourself, with any camera
questions.fact: Robert Cornelius, an American photography pioneer, took it, and wrote on the back that it was 'the first light picture ever taken'.

questions.question: How many teeth does a child have before the adult ones come?
questions.fact: There are five in each quarter of the mouth, ten in each jaw.

questions.question: How many bones are in one human hand?
questions.fact: 14 are in the fingers and thumb, 5 in the palm and 8 in the wrist.

questions.question: What is the population of London?
questions.fact: That's 13.1% of the UK's people, and its wider metropolitan area holds 15.4 million.

questions.question: How tall are the big standing stones of Stonehenge?
questions.fact: Each weighs around 25 tons, with a lintel stone laid across the tops.

questions.question: How many people can Glastonbury Festival take?
questions.fact: The first festival at Worthy Farm drew 1,500 people.

questions.question: How many international visitors did Bangkok get?
questions.fact: Hong Kong came next with 23.2 million.

source.title: List of cities by international visitors

questions.question: How many medals has Norway won at the Winter Olympics?
questions.fact: That's the most of any country, ahead of the United States with 363.

questions.question: How many sites does Italy have on UNESCO's World Heritage List?
questions.fact: That's the most of any country, with China one behind on 61.

questions.question: How far does the Sahara stretch from the Atlantic to the Red Sea?
questions.fact: From north to south it is 1,800 km.

questions.question: How many bones are in a giraffe's neck?
questions.fact: Like most mammals, including us, it has seven: a giraffe's are just much longer.

questions.question: How much of Iceland is covered by plants?
questions.fact: Lakes and glaciers cover another 14.3% of its surface.

questions.question: How much of the Alps lies in Switzerland?
questions.fact: Austria has the biggest share, 28.7%, then Italy with 27.2% and France with 21.4%.

questions.question: How much of your body weight is your brain?
questions.fact: Yet it receives 15% of the blood the heart pumps out.

questions.question: How many matches does each Premier League club play in a league season?
questions.fact: Erling Haaland holds the record for goals in one of those seasons: 36.

How long is the Channel Tunnel between England and France?
questions.fact: Its 37.9 km under the sea is the longest underwater stretch of any tunnel in the world.

questions.question: How long is the Panama Canal?
questions.fact: Locks lift ships some 27 m up to Gatun Lake, a man-made lake, to cross the isthmus.

questions.question: How many countries does the Danube flow through or along?
questions.fact: On its way from Germany to the Black Sea it passes four capitals: Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade.

questions.question: How many countries have won the men's football World Cup?
questions.fact: Each winner wears a star on its badge for every title it has won.

questions.question: How many teeth does a grown dog have?
questions.fact: They are built for meat: dogs use their carnassial teeth to cut it into bite-sized chunks.

questions.question: How many episodes of Friends were made?
questions.fact: Its ten seasons averaged about two dozen episodes each.

questions.question: How many bicycles are there in the Netherlands?
questions.fact: That's 1.3 for every Dutch person old enough to ride, on 35,000 km of cycle paths.

questions.question: How fast has a car ever gone?
questions.definition: the land speed record, a jet-powered car
questions.fact: ThrustSSC is the only car ever to have officially broken the sound barrier.

questions.question: How fast has a train ever gone?
questions.definition: the record, with people on board
questions.fact: Japan's L0 maglev runs on rubber wheels at low speed, then floats on its magnets.

questions.question: How old was the oldest cat on record?
questions.fact: Her owner credited a diet including turkey bacon, broccoli, coffee with cream and an eyedropper of red wine.

questions.question: How long did Louis XIV, the longest-reigning monarch in history, reign?
questions.fact: He became king of France at four, when his father died, and reigned until his own death at 76.

questions.question: How fast does a person walk, on average?
questions.fact: That's 1.4 metres a second, the speed road design guides use for people crossing the street.

questions.question: How deep is the Grand Canyon?
questions.fact: The Colorado River carved it 446 km long and up to 29 km wide.

questions.question: How many blocks of stone went into the Great Pyramid of Giza?
questions.fact: Together they weigh about 6 million tonnes.

questions.question: How long is the record for sailing around the world?
questions.definition: with a crew, the Jules Verne Trophy, 2026
questions.fact: The trophy for it is named after Jules Verne, whose hero went round the world in 80 days.

questions.question: How long is the island of Manhattan, end to end?
questions.fact: At its widest, near 14th Street, it's only 3.7 km across.

questions.question: How tall are young Dutch men, among the world's tallest, on average?
questions.fact: Before 1850, men in Leiden averaged only 167 cm.

questions.question: How many steps did the first visitors climb to the top of the Eiffel Tower?
questions.fact: Nearly 30,000 people made the climb before the lifts opened.

questions.question: How many keys does a full-size computer keyboard have?
questions.fact: Outside the US the norm is one key more.

questions.question: How many people live in Venice's historic island city?
questions.fact: Most of the city's 249,385 people live on the mainland instead.

questions.question: How fast is the fastest wind ever measured in a tornado?
questions.fact: A tornado needs winds of only 64 km/h at the ground to count as one.

questions.question: How long is Chile from north to south?
questions.fact: Squeezed between the Andes and the Pacific, it is the southernmost country in the world.

questions.question: How deep is the ocean on average?
questions.fact: Over 70.8% of Earth's surface, that adds up to 1.335 billion cubic kilometres of water.

questions.question: How heavy is the average top-division sumo wrestler?
questions.fact: There are no weight classes, so a wrestler can face an opponent twice his weight.

questions.question: How much beer is drunk at Oktoberfest?
questions.fact: A record 7.2 million visitors came that year, about a litre of beer each.

questions.question: How many missions did NASA's Space Shuttles fly?
questions.fact: Five orbiters shared them over 30 years, launching the Hubble Space Telescope among much else.

questions.question: How long did Apollo 11 take, from launch to splashdown?
questions.fact: Armstrong and Aldrin spent 2 hours 31 minutes walking outside on the Moon.

questions.question: How long did Lindbergh's New York to Paris flight take?
questions.definition: the first solo flight across the Atlantic
questions.fact: He flew about 5,800 km alone, in a small single-engine plane.

questions.question: How many countries in the EU use the euro?
questions.fact: Six EU members still keep their own money, among them Sweden, Poland and Denmark.

questions.question: How wide is the Strait of Gibraltar at its narrowest?
questions.fact: That is all that separates Europe from Africa, over water 900 m deep.

questions.question: How long is Hadrian's Wall, the Roman wall across northern England?
questions.fact: It was 80 Roman miles long, built to separate the Romans from the barbarians.

questions.question: How many people visit the Louvre, the world's most visited museum?
questions.fact: The Mona Lisa alone draws about 20,000 visitors a day.

questions.question: How much of Japan is mountainous?
questions.fact: A mountain range runs through each of its main islands.

questions.question: What share of Indonesians live on Java?
questions.fact: Java is the world's most populous island, with only 7% of Indonesia's land.

questions.question: What share of the UK's people live in England?
questions.fact: England's 56.3 million people make it by far the most populous of the UK's four nations.

questions.question: What share of the world's coffee is arabica?
questions.fact: Packs labelled 100% Arabica sell it as a mark of quality over the cheaper robusta.

questions.question: How much of Finland is forest?
questions.fact: Another 10% is lakes, rivers and ponds.

questions.question: What share of mammal species are rodents?
questions.fact: They live on every continent but Antarctica, and most kinds weigh less than 100 g.

questions.question: How much of a person's weight is bone?
questions.fact: That's about 10 to 11 kg for an average person, heaviest between the ages of 25 and 30.

questions.question: What share of Japan's people are 65 or older?
questions.fact: That's the highest share among the 38 countries in Japan's own statistics report.

questions.question: How much of California is covered by forest?
questions.fact: No other US state has as many kinds of pine.

questions.question: How much of Greece's land is on its islands?
questions.fact: The other 83.33%, 110,496 square kilometres, is mainland.

questions.question: How much of Africa does the Sahara cover?
questions.fact: At 9.2 million square kilometres it is the largest hot desert in the world.

questions.question: How much of the world's cocoa does Ivory Coast grow?
questions.fact: With Ghana next door, the two grow about 58% of the world's cocoa.

questions.question: What share of Canadians speak French as their first language?
questions.fact: In Quebec, 85% of people are native French speakers.

questions.question: What share of the Swiss speak German as their main language?
questions.fact: French comes next with 22.7%, then Italian with 8.2% and Romansh with 0.5%.

questions.question: How much of the world's land lies under glacier ice?
questions.fact: Almost all of it is the ice sheets of the polar regions, which hold 99% of all glacier ice.

questions.question: How much of the Amazon rainforest has been cut down?
questions.fact: Another 6% has been highly degraded.

questions.question: How much of the Dead Sea's water is salt?
questions.fact: That's 9.6 times as salty as the ocean, which makes swimming in it like floating.

questions.question: What share of your body's mass is oxygen?
questions.fact: Most of it is in water; carbon comes next with 18.5%.

questions.question: How much of 18-carat gold is pure gold?
questions.fact: Carats count parts of gold in 24, so 24-carat gold is pure.

questions.question: What share of the Sun is hydrogen?
questions.fact: Nearly all the rest is helium, 24.85%.

questions.question: How much of Earth's land is in Asia?
questions.fact: Its 4.7 billion people are about 60% of the world's population.

questions.question: How much of Europe's land is in Russia?
questions.fact: Yet that European part is only about 23% of Russia's own territory.

questions.question: What share of the world's surface fresh water is in the Great Lakes?
questions.fact: Spread over North America, it would cover the whole continent 1.5 metres deep.

questions.question: How much of honey is water?
questions.fact: It starts as flower nectar that is 70 to 80% water.

questions.question: How much of sea-level air pressure is left at the top of Everest?
questions.fact: Strong winds can lower it further, cutting the oxygen available by up to 14 percent.

questions.question: How much of the world's sugar comes from sugarcane?
questions.fact: Most of the rest is made from sugar beets.

questions.question: How much of the world's desert is sand?
questions.fact: It ranges from 2% in North America to over 45% in Central Asia.

questions.question: How much of Australia is arid or semi-arid?
questions.fact: About 95% of Australians live within 100 km of the coast.

questions.question: When did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.fact: East Germany's government announced one evening that its citizens could visit the West.

questions.question: When was Google founded?
questions.fact: Larry Page and Sergey Brin set up the search engine in a friend's garage.

questions.question: When was Wikipedia launched?
questions.fact: It began as a side project to feed Nupedia, an online encyclopedia written by experts.

questions.question: When did the first Pokémon games come out?
questions.fact: They were Pocket Monsters Red and Green, for the Game Boy.

questions.question: When did Sony's first PlayStation go on sale?
questions.fact: Its games sold 962 million copies in all.

questions.question: When did Instagram launch?
questions.fact: Its name joins instant camera and telegram.

questions.question: When did Yuri Gagarin become the first person in space?
questions.fact: His flight took 108 minutes from launch to landing, once around the Earth.

questions.question: When did Alexander Graham Bell patent the telephone?
questions.fact: His research on hearing and speech led him to it.

questions.question: When were the first Nobel Prizes awarded?
questions.fact: They marked the fifth anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death.

questions.question: When did someone first run a mile in under four minutes?
questions.fact: Roger Bannister ran 3:59.4 at Oxford, aged 25, with two friends as pacemakers.

questions.question: When was the first Barbie doll sold?
questions.fact: She wore a black-and-white zebra-striped swimsuit and cost three dollars.

questions.question: When did the Golden Gate Bridge open?
questions.fact: It was the longest and the tallest suspension bridge in the world when it opened.

questions.question: When was the first baby conceived by IVF born?
questions.fact: Louise Brown was born in Oldham, England, by planned caesarean.

questions.question: When did anyone first reach the South Pole?
questions.fact: Roald Amundsen's party got there five weeks ahead of Robert Falcon Scott's.

questions.question: When were X-rays discovered?
questions.fact: Wilhelm Röntgen called them X for unknown, and took an X-ray of his wife's hand within weeks.

questions.question: When was the Rosetta Stone found?
questions.fact: A French army officer found it during France's invasion of Egypt.

questions.question: When was the first dinosaur named?
questions.fact: It was Megalosaurus, named by William Buckland.

questions.question: When did Darwin publish On the Origin of Species?
questions.fact: He had been working on the theory for about 20 years before he published it.

questions.question: When was television first shown to the public?
questions.definition: John Logie Baird's real pictures, not silhouettes
questions.fact: Months earlier Baird had sent his first greyscale picture: the head of a ventriloquist's dummy.

questions.question: When did the first voyage around the world end?
questions.fact: Magellan himself died on the way, in the Philippines; Juan Sebastián Elcano brought the crew home.

questions.question: When did the Leaning Tower of Pisa start to lean?
questions.fact: It began to sink once building had reached the second floor.

questions.question: When was the first postage stamp, the Penny Black, issued?
questions.fact: It showed Queen Victoria's head.

questions.question: When were riveted denim jeans patented?
questions.fact: Jacob Davis asked Levi Strauss to help him apply for the patent, and they shared it.

questions.question: When was the first crossword published?
questions.fact: Arthur Wynne, a Liverpool-born journalist, printed his word-cross in the New York World.

questions.question: When was the bikini introduced?
questions.fact: Louis Réard named it after Bikini Atoll, where a nuclear bomb had been tested four days before.

questions.question: When did the Boeing 747 jumbo jet first fly?
questions.fact: It was certified that December, ready to carry passengers for Pan Am.

questions.question: When did the first CDs go on sale?
questions.fact: The CD was the second optical disc to reach the market, after the bigger LaserDisc.

questions.question: When did Concorde make its last passenger flight?
questions.fact: Rising costs and fewer passengers ended it, 27 years after it entered service.

questions.question: When were the first Academy Awards held?
questions.fact: The ceremony lasted 15 minutes, at a dinner for about 270 people.

questions.question: When did the Chernobyl disaster happen?
questions.fact: The fire in reactor 4 burned for about two weeks.

questions.question: When did the first Disneyland open?
questions.fact: It was the only park built under Walt Disney's own supervision.

questions.question: How many tiles are in a standard set of dominoes?
questions.fact: There is one tile for each pair of ends from blank to six, up to the double six.

questions.question: How many Earths would fit inside Jupiter?
questions.fact: It is the largest planet in the Solar System, 142,976 km across at its equator.

questions.question: How many languages are official at the United Nations?
questions.fact: They are Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish, each equally authoritative.

source.title: Official languages of the United Nations

questions.question: How many countries are there in Central America?
questions.fact: Between Mexico and Colombia: Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Panama.

questions.question: How fast do people type on a phone, on average?
questions.fact: Professional typists on a real keyboard manage 43 to 80 words a minute.

questions.question: How many people use Shinjuku Station, the world's busiest, each day?
questions.fact: That makes it the world's busiest railway station by far, says Guinness World Records.

questions.question: How long was Route 66, from Chicago to Los Angeles?
questions.fact: It crossed eight states on its way from Chicago to Santa Monica, on the Pacific.

questions.question: How fast was the Titanic going when its lookouts saw the iceberg?
questions.fact: Seven ice warnings had come in, but full speed in icy waters was standard practice then.

questions.question: How long does the average person in the world live?
questions.fact: At the start of the 19th century, no country in the world had a life expectancy above 40.

questions.question: How long did Usain Bolt take to run 200 m in his world record?
questions.fact: That's an average of 37.52 km/h over the whole race.

questions.question: How long does a chicken's egg take to hatch?
questions.fact: The chick breaks out of the shell with a little egg tooth on its beak.

questions.question: How much of your height is your thigh bone?
questions.fact: The femur is the longest bone in the body, and the ratio holds for men and women alike.

questions.question: When did the Beatles break up?
questions.fact: They had stopped touring four years before, after over 1,400 concerts, and ended as a studio band.

questions.question: When was the first Wimbledon tennis championship played?
questions.fact: Only men's singles was played, by 22 men who each paid a guinea to enter.

questions.question: When was the first Eurovision Song Contest?
questions.fact: Seven countries took part, each with two songs, the only time more than one entry was allowed.

questions.question: When did Pac-Man first come out?
questions.fact: It was first called Puck Man, and was tested in an arcade in Shibuya, Tokyo.

questions.question: When were the first Paralympic Games held?
questions.fact: 400 athletes from 23 nations competed in Rome, alongside the Olympics.

questions.question: When did Edward Jenner make the first vaccine?
questions.fact: He showed that catching mild cowpox protected people from deadly smallpox.

questions.question: How long did the Wright brothers' first powered flight last?
questions.fact: Orville covered 37 m at only 10.9 km/h over the ground.

questions.question: How many episodes of Game of Thrones were made?
questions.fact: The plan was for each novel to give a season's worth of episodes.

questions.question: How long does the London Eye take to go round once?
questions.fact: It moves at 26 cm a second, slow enough to step on and off without stopping.

questions.question: How many people and organisations have won a Nobel Prize?
questions.fact: The prizes have been given 633 times, many of them shared.

questions.question: How far has a car gone in the 24 Hours of Le Mans?
questions.fact: That's about 18 times the length of a Formula One Grand Prix.

questions.question: How many countries have no coastline?
questions.fact: Two, Liechtenstein and Uzbekistan, are doubly landlocked, surrounded only by landlocked countries.

questions.question: How long did the first flight round the world without refuelling take?
questions.fact: Dick Rutan stayed at the controls without relief for almost the first three days.

questions.question: How long can a total eclipse of the Sun last, at most?
questions.fact: Observers aboard Concorde once stretched one to about 74 minutes by chasing the Moon's shadow.

questions.question: How much caffeine is in a shot of espresso?
questions.fact: Espresso is stronger than filter coffee, but a big mug of filter has more caffeine in all.

questions.question: How many squares are there on a Scrabble board?
questions.fact: The English set's 100 tiles include two blanks worth no points.

questions.question: How long does the Eurostar take from London to Paris?
questions.fact: When it began, from Waterloo, the trip took 2 hours 55 minutes.

questions.question: How many homes are there in the UK?
questions.fact: About 23 million of them are in England.

questions.question: How many skyscrapers does Hong Kong have?
questions.fact: That's the most of any city, ahead of Shenzhen and New York.

source.title: List of cities with the most skyscrapers

questions.question: How long was the Berlin Wall around West Berlin?
questions.fact: Its last version was built from 45,000 concrete sections, each 3.6 m high.

questions.question: How long is the ring of the Large Hadron Collider?
questions.fact: It runs up to 175 m beneath the border of France and Switzerland, near Geneva.

questions.question: How often does Old Faithful, the Yellowstone geyser, erupt?
questions.fact: Each eruption lasts 1.5 to 5 minutes and throws up 14,000 to 32,000 litres of boiling water.

questions.question: How high above sea level is the Maldives, on average?
questions.fact: Its highest natural point is only 2.4 m, making it the world's lowest-lying country.

questions.question: How many rooms does Buckingham Palace have?
questions.fact: Its garden is the largest private garden in London.

questions.question: How many lifeboats did the Titanic carry?
questions.fact: Together they could hold only a little over half of the 2,207 people on board.

questions.question: Name a country with 8 land borders
questions.definition: France has 11, counting its overseas territories

questions.definition: France has 11, counting its overseas territories

Name a US state with about the same area as Wales

questions.fact: New Jersey is within 7% of the size of Wales.

questions.question: Name a US state with about the same area as England
questions.definition: total area, lakes and coastal water included
questions.fact: Alabama, Louisiana and Arkansas are each within 4% of England's area.

questions.question: Name a US state with about the same area as the UK
questions.definition: total area, lakes and coastal water included
questions.fact: Michigan, Wyoming and Oregon are each within 5% of the UK's area.

questions.question: Name a US state with about the same area as Germany
questions.definition: total area, lakes and coastal water included
questions.fact: Montana, the fourth-biggest state, is 6.5% bigger than Germany.

questions.question: How many ribs does a person have?
questions.fact: Twelve pairs: when Vesalius counted 24 in 1543 it caused a stir, as many believed from the Adam and Eve story that men had one fewer.

questions.question: How long does a taste bud last before it's replaced?
questions.fact: A tongue has thousands of them, sitting on the small bumps called papillae.

questions.question: How long does a yawn last?
questions.fact: It's a long breath in as the mouth slowly opens, a brief stretch at the peak, then a quick breath out.

questions.question: How much water can a thirsty camel drink in one go?
questions.fact: It drinks 10 to 20 litres a minute, and can lose more than 30% of its body's water, which would kill most mammals.

questions.question: How much weight does a newborn blue whale gain each day?
questions.fact: Its mother makes an estimated 220 kg of milk a day to keep it growing.

questions.question: How long is a red kangaroo's pregnancy?
questions.fact: The tiny newborn then grows in its mother's pouch, leaving it for good after about 235 days.

questions.question: How many volts can an electric eel's shock reach?
questions.fact: That makes it the strongest electricity maker in nature, enough to stun the fish it hunts.

questions.question: How long does a male emperor penguin fast to raise his egg?
questions.fact: He balances the egg on his feet, under loose skin and feathers, for 65 to 75 days until it hatches.

questions.question: How far away can you hear a lion's roar?
questions.fact: Lions roar most often at night, to let other lions know where they are.

questions.question: How many species of bear are there?
questions.fact: The polar bear is mostly a meat-eater and the giant panda mostly a plant-eater; the other six eat both.

questions.question: How many claws are on a cat's four paws?
questions.fact: Most cats have five claws on each front paw and four on each back one.

questions.question: How long does a wild sloth sleep each day?
questions.definition: three-toed sloths, measured in the wild
questions.fact: They spend 90 percent of their time motionless, and digesting a meal can take a month or more.

questions.question: How long does a koala sleep each day?
questions.fact: Its diet of eucalyptus leaves gives so little energy that digesting it can take 100 hours.

questions.question: How long can a common swift stay in the air without landing?
questions.fact: Swifts never land on the ground by choice, where they would be easy prey.

questions.question: How much milk does a dairy cow give a day?
questions.fact: Most cows are milked twice a day, and the milk is taken to a dairy to be processed.

questions.question: How many customers does McDonald's serve worldwide each day?
questions.fact: They come to about 41,800 restaurants around the world.

questions.question: How many baguettes do the French eat a day?
questions.fact: Algeria eats even more: about 49 million baguettes a day.

questions.question: How many films are in the official James Bond series?
questions.fact: Eon made all but two of the Bond films ever released.

questions.question: How many words did Dr. Seuss use to write Green Eggs and Ham?
questions.fact: His editor bet him he couldn't write a good children's book with so few, and 'not' turns up 82 times.

questions.question: How many people saw Taylor Swift's Eras Tour in person?
questions.fact: It played 51 cities in 21 countries, on five continents.

questions.question: How long are the three Lord of the Rings films back to back?
questions.fact: The extended editions released for home viewing run over 11 hours.

source.title: The Lord of the Rings (film series)

questions.question: How long did Michelangelo take to paint the Sistine Chapel ceiling?
questions.fact: He painted it standing on scaffolding, not lying on his back, as one early biographer imagined.

questions.question: How old was Mozart when he began composing?
questions.fact: He played his little pieces to his father, who wrote them down for him.

questions.question: How many syllables does a traditional haiku have?
questions.fact: In Japanese it counts sound units called on, in three phrases of five, seven and five.

questions.question: How many points does the maple leaf on Canada's flag have?
questions.fact: The number means nothing: wind tunnel tests showed this design blurred least in a strong wind.

questions.question: How many stars are on the European Union's flag?
questions.fact: The number never changes: twelve is meant as a symbol of perfection and entirety.

questions.question: How many blocks are in a game of Jenga?
questions.fact: They start as a tower of 18 layers, three blocks each; the name comes from a Swahili word meaning 'to build'.

questions.question: How many letters are in the Greek alphabet?
questions.fact: The same letters, from alpha to omega, have been standard since the end of the 4th century BC.

questions.question: How many languages are official in the European Union?
questions.fact: That's fewer than its 27 members, as Austria, Belgium and Luxembourg brought no language of their own.

questions.question: How many strings does a concert harp have?
questions.fact: Most are white, but the C strings are red and the F strings black or blue.

questions.question: How many holes are in a Connect Four grid?
questions.fact: Computers have solved the game: with the right moves, the first player can always win.

questions.question: How long did Tolkien take to write The Lord of the Rings?
questions.fact: It began as a sequel to The Hobbit and became one of the best-selling books ever, with over 150 million copies sold.

questions.question: How many feathers make a badminton shuttlecock?
questions.fact: Makers use feathers from only right wings or only left wings in each one, as the two are shaped differently.

questions.question: How many laps of the track is the 10,000 metres race?
questions.fact: It's the longest standard track race; the men's world record is 26 minutes 11 seconds.

questions.question: How old was the oldest Olympic medal winner?
questions.definition: not counting the old art contests
questions.fact: Oscar Swahn, a Swedish shooter, won silver; he is also the oldest gold medallist ever, at 64.

questions.question: How many medals did Michael Phelps win at the Olympics?
questions.fact: 23 of them were gold, over four Olympic Games: more medals than any other athlete.

questions.question: How many goals did Lionel Messi score for Barcelona?
questions.fact: It's the most anyone has scored for a single club, and 474 of them came in La Liga.

questions.question: How many people in the US watched the 2025 Super Bowl?
questions.fact: It was the most watched broadcast in American television history, beating the Super Bowl the year before.

questions.question: How far is an Ironman triathlon, swim, ride and run together?
questions.fact: It's a 3.9 km swim, then a 180.2 km bike ride, then a full marathon.

questions.question: What is the highest score possible in a game of ten-pin bowling?
questions.fact: It takes 12 strikes in a row: one in each of the first nine frames and three in the tenth.

questions.question: What is the highest break possible in snooker, normally?
questions.fact: Joe Davis made the first official one; Ronnie O'Sullivan's fastest took 5 minutes and 8 seconds.

questions.question: How old was Pelé when he won his first World Cup?
questions.fact: He is the only player to win three World Cups, and still the youngest to win one.

questions.question: How many stages does the Tour de France have?
questions.fact: Each is a day's racing, spread over 23 or 24 days.

questions.question: How many events awarded medals at the Paris 2024 Olympics?
questions.fact: They spanned 32 sports, at the first Games with equal numbers of men and women competing.

questions.question: How far is the official ski jumping world record?
questions.fact: Ryōyū Kobayashi flew 291 m at an unofficial event in Iceland, which doesn't count.

questions.question: How many yellow taxis are licensed in New York City?
questions.fact: The city sold no new licences for about 60 years, so by 2014 one cost over $1 million.

questions.question: How many people visited Disney World's Magic Kingdom in 2024?
questions.fact: It has been the most visited theme park in the world for 18 years running.

questions.question: How many songs could the first iPod hold?
questions.definition: on its 5 GB hard drive, as MP3s
questions.fact: It cost $399 and had a black-and-white screen.

questions.question: How long did the Mayflower take to cross the Atlantic?
questions.definition: England to first sight of land
questions.fact: When land finally came into sight, it turned out to be Cape Cod.

questions.question: How long did a Pony Express letter take from Missouri to California?
questions.fact: Riders changed horses every 16 to 24 km and rode day and night, but the service lasted only 18 months.

questions.question: How long has the longest-burning light bulb been on?
questions.fact: It was a 60-watt bulb and now glows about as bright as a 4-watt nightlight.

questions.question: How many pixels does a 4K TV screen have?
questions.fact: It's 3,840 across by 2,160 down, four times as many as a 1080p HD screen.

questions.question: How often does lightning strike the Empire State Building in a year?
questions.fact: Planes are struck often too, though strikes are generally not dangerous to them.

questions.question: How wide would a cube of all the world's gold be?
questions.fact: That cube would weigh about 201,296 tonnes.

questions.question: How many moves are always enough to solve a Rubik's Cube?
questions.fact: Computers provided by Google proved it, and millions of positions need every one of those moves.

questions.question: How many frames a second does cinema film run at?
questions.fact: Silent-film theatres ran at 22 to 26, so sound films settled on this as a compromise.

questions.question: How long did it take to build Cologne Cathedral?
questions.definition: the Gothic one, start to finish
questions.fact: Work stopped for about 280 years in the middle, and when it was finished it was the tallest building in the world.

questions.question: How long did it take to carve Mount Rushmore?
questions.fact: About 400 workers used dynamite, then drilled close-set holes and chipped the rest away by hand.

questions.question: How heavy is Big Ben, the great bell in London's clock tower?
questions.fact: Big Ben is the bell's nickname; four smaller bells beside it chime the quarter hours.

questions.question: How long did the Sydney Opera House take to build?
questions.definition: first work on site to opening
questions.fact: It opened 16 years after Jørn Utzon won the design competition, after huge cost and time overruns.

questions.question: How long are the Pentagon's corridors, all added together?
questions.fact: It has five sides, five floors above ground and five ring corridors on each floor.

questions.question: How many people can stand inside St Peter's Basilica in Rome?
questions.fact: Seated, it holds 20,000.

questions.question: How many Earths would fit side by side between Earth and the Moon?
questions.fact: Flying that far on Earth, non-stop, would take a plane more than two weeks.

questions.question: How often does Halley's Comet come back?
questions.fact: Edmond Halley saw that three famous comets were one object returning, the first comet known to come back.

questions.question: How much Moon rock did the Apollo astronauts bring back?
questions.fact: It came in 2,200 samples from six landings; Apollo 17 alone brought back 110 kg.

questions.question: How thick are Saturn's main rings?
questions.fact: They're almost pure water ice, and may be much younger than Saturn itself.

questions.question: How high did Felix Baumgartner jump from in his record skydive?
questions.fact: He broke the sound barrier on the way down, at 1,357.64 km/h, with no engine.

questions.question: How far from Earth does the James Webb Space Telescope orbit?
questions.fact: That's about four times as far as the Moon, at a spot where the Sun, Earth and Moon all stay behind its sunshield.

questions.question: How wide was the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs?
questions.fact: It struck what is now Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula, and its crater lies buried about a kilometre down.

questions.question: How much rain falls a year in Mawsynram, often called the wettest place?
questions.fact: Two towns in Colombia report even more, so its title is disputed.

questions.question: How old is the oldest known living tree?
questions.fact: It's a bristlecone pine called Methuselah, in California's White Mountains, and its exact spot was kept secret for years.

questions.question: How thick is Antarctica's ice sheet, on average?
questions.fact: If it all melted, sea levels around the world would rise by almost 60 metres.

questions.question: How many countries are members of the United Nations?
questions.fact: Every member has one vote in the General Assembly, and only one has ever tried to leave on its own.

source.title: Member states of the United Nations

questions.question: How many countries does the equator pass through?
questions.fact: It also crosses the seas of three more: the Maldives, Kiribati and the United States.

questions.question: How many passengers used the world's busiest airport in 2025?
questions.fact: It's Atlanta's Hartsfield–Jackson, top of the list every year since the late 1990s but one.

source.title: List of busiest airports by passenger traffic

questions.question: How many golf courses are there in the United States?
questions.fact: The United States has over 40% of all the golf courses in the world.

questions.question: How many flowers can join together to form one pineapple?
questions.fact: They fuse into one 'multiple fruit', and the plant usually matures within a year.

questions.question: How many visitors a day can climb to the Statue of Liberty's crown?
questions.fact: Tickets can be reserved up to five months ahead, in groups of up to four.

questions.question: How many spectators did Rome's Colosseum typically hold?
questions.fact: It hosted gladiator fights, animal hunts, dramas and even mock sea battles.

questions.question: How long does your body take to make a new red blood cell?
questions.fact: Each one then circulates in the blood for three to four months.

questions.question: What share of people are right-eye dominant?
questions.fact: About 29% favour the left eye instead.

questions.question: What share of the world's people are short-sighted?
questions.fact: That's about 1.5 billion people, and in parts of China and Malaysia it's up to 41% of adults.

questions.question: How much of your blood is plasma, the pale yellow liquid part?
questions.fact: Plasma is mostly water, up to 95%, and gets its yellow from substances such as bilirubin.

questions.question: What share of the world's people have brown eyes?
questions.fact: Blue eyes come next, at 8 to 10%, and green is the rarest, at about 2%.

questions.question: At any moment, how much of your blood is in your veins?
questions.fact: And nearly three-quarters of that sits in the smallest veins and venules.

questions.question: How much of the world's food do rice, maize and wheat make up?
questions.fact: Just 15 crops provide 90% of the food energy people get from plants, and rice alone feeds almost half of humanity.

questions.question: How much of the world's soy is fed to farm animals?
questions.fact: Dried soybeans are 36% protein, which makes the meal left after pressing out the oil a cheap animal feed.

questions.question: How much of Italy's milk goes into making Parmesan?
questions.fact: That's about 3.6 million wheels a year, and each vat of 1,100 litres of milk makes just two.

questions.question: How much of the world's land is used for farming?
questions.fact: Over two-thirds of it is pasture for grazing animals, and less than a third grows crops.

questions.question: How much of all the plastic ever made has been recycled?
questions.fact: Of the plastic thrown away, 12% was burned and 79% went to landfill or into the environment.

questions.question: How much of France's electricity comes from nuclear power?
questions.fact: France has 56 power reactors, all run by EDF, the state-owned electricity company.

questions.question: How much of Iceland's electricity comes from geothermal power?
questions.fact: Almost all the rest comes from hydropower, though 90% of homes are heated with geothermal water.

questions.question: How much of Earth is covered by cloud at any moment?
questions.fact: Clouds cover about 72% of the oceans but only about 55% of the land.

questions.question: How much of the river water entering the oceans comes from the Amazon?
questions.fact: It carries more water than the next seven largest rivers combined.

questions.question: How much of the world's dry land is mountainous?
questions.fact: Mountains cover 33% of Eurasia but only 14% of Africa.

questions.question: How much of Earth's surface lies in the tropics?
questions.fact: About 40% of the world's people live there too, a share expected to reach half by 2050.

questions.question: How much of the Moon is covered by its dark 'seas'?
questions.fact: They're old lava plains, dark because of their iron, and nearly all are on the side that faces Earth.

questions.question: How wide is the Moon, as a share of Earth's width?
questions.fact: At 3,474 km across, it's about as wide as the contiguous United States.

questions.question: What share of spacecraft sent to Mars have failed?
questions.fact: The early ones fared worst: the Soviet Union's first nine probes meant for Mars all failed.

questions.question: What share of an octopus's neurons are in its arms?
questions.fact: It has over 500 million neurons, about as many as a dog, and the ones in its arms let each arm act on its own.

questions.question: What share of Australia's mammal species live nowhere else?
questions.fact: For its reptiles the share is even higher, 93%, and for its amphibians 94%.

questions.question: What share of bird species are perching birds?
questions.fact: Their toes, three forward and one back, lock onto a branch, so they can sleep perched without falling off.

questions.question: What share of the world's dogs roam free, not as pets?
questions.fact: Only 17 to 24% of dogs live as pets in rich countries, out of 700 to 900 million in all.

questions.question: What share of the world's wild tigers live in India?
questions.fact: India counted 3,682 wild tigers, more than double its count of 1,706 twelve years earlier.

questions.question: What share of the world's people can read and write?
questions.fact: Two hundred years ago it was 12%.

questions.question: What share of all Wikipedia articles are in English?
questions.fact: English still has more articles than any other edition, about 7.27 million.

questions.question: What share of people in Wales can speak Welsh?
questions.fact: Just over a quarter said they had at least some Welsh.

questions.question: What share of the world's adults have a bank or mobile-money account?
questions.fact: That still leaves about 1.3 billion adults without one.

questions.question: What share of new cars sold worldwide in 2025 were electric?
questions.fact: Over 20 million were sold, yet electric cars were only about 5% of all the cars on the road.

questions.question: What share of Americans hold a passport?
questions.fact: In 1990 it was just 5%.

questions.question: What share of the world's people are under 15?
questions.fact: People aged 65 and over made up nearly a tenth.

questions.question: What share of the world's people live less than 150 km from the sea?
questions.fact: Many big cities grew up on good harbours, and some inland ones dug canals to become ports.

questions.question: How much of the Ming-era Great Wall of China has disappeared?
questions.fact: Many of the square lookout towers in its most famous pictures have gone too.

questions.question: When did women first take part in the Olympics?
questions.fact: 22 women competed, and Charlotte Cooper, a British tennis player, became the first female individual champion.

source.title: Participation of women in the Olympics

questions.question: When was the first London Marathon run?
questions.fact: 6,255 runners finished, and the men's race ended in a tie, the two leaders crossing the line holding hands.

questions.question: When did William Herschel discover Uranus?
questions.fact: He spotted it from his garden in Bath with a homemade telescope, and at first reported it as a comet.

questions.question: When did James Naismith invent basketball?
questions.fact: A PE teacher, he made it up to keep his class busy on a rainy day, with peach baskets for hoops.

questions.question: When was the first Formula One World Championship held?
questions.fact: It had seven races, and one of them was the Indianapolis 500.

questions.question: When did the Olympics start giving gold, silver and bronze medals?
questions.fact: At the first modern Games, winners got a silver medal and an olive branch.

questions.question: When was insulin first used to treat diabetes?
questions.fact: Frederick Banting and Charles Best first gave it to patients in Toronto, Canada.

questions.question: When did Bayer start selling aspirin?
questions.fact: Its name comes from Spiraea, the meadowsweet plant its key ingredient was first taken from.

questions.question: When was the stethoscope invented?
questions.fact: René Laennec made it because he wasn't comfortable putting his ear to a woman's chest.

questions.question: When did the Suez Canal open?
questions.fact: It opened under French control, as a single-lane waterway with a few places for ships to pass.

questions.question: When did building start on Barcelona's Sagrada Família?
questions.fact: It's still under construction, paid for only by private donations; Gaudí said his client was not in a hurry.

questions.question: When did London's Tower Bridge open?
questions.fact: Its high walkways between the towers were so little used, except by pickpockets, that they closed for over 70 years.

questions.question: When was the Voyager 1 space probe launched?
questions.fact: It went up 16 days after its twin, Voyager 2, and still sends data from beyond the Sun's heliosphere.

questions.question: When was Earthrise, the photo of Earth rising over the Moon, taken?
questions.fact: William Anders took it on Christmas Eve, from Apollo 8, the first crewed voyage to orbit the Moon.

questions.question: When did someone first walk in space?
questions.fact: Alexei Leonov spent 12 minutes outside his spacecraft, Voskhod 2.

questions.question: When did the first crew move into the International Space Station?
questions.fact: They stayed 136 days, starting a human presence on the station that hasn't been broken since.

questions.question: When did Sony launch the Walkman, its portable cassette player?
questions.fact: Sony expected to sell 5,000 a month and sold more than 30,000 in the first two months.

questions.question: When did Toy Story, the first computer-animated feature film, come out?
questions.fact: It was Pixar's first feature film, and it grossed over $363 million worldwide.

questions.question: When was the first Christmas card printed for sale?
questions.fact: Sir Henry Cole, a civil servant in London, commissioned it from the artist John Callcott Horsley.

questions.question: When was the first bicycle, pushed along with the feet, invented?
questions.fact: Karl Drais called it a 'running machine': he wanted a way to get about without a horse.

questions.question: When was food in tin cans first patented?
questions.fact: Peter Durand's patent built on Nicolas Appert's finding that food sealed in jars didn't spoil.

questions.question: When was the last widely accepted sighting of a dodo?
questions.fact: Dutch sailors had first recorded the bird on Mauritius in 1598.

questions.question: When was Dolly the sheep, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, born?
questions.fact: She had three mothers: one gave the egg, one the DNA, and one carried her.

questions.question: When did the last known Tasmanian tiger die?
questions.fact: It died at Hobart Zoo, 59 days after the species was finally given legal protection.

questions.question: When did Mickey Mouse make his official debut?
questions.fact: It was one of the first cartoons with fully synchronised sound.

questions.question: When did the Guinness Book of Records first come out?
questions.fact: Sir Hugh Beaver came up with it to settle arguments in pubs, and it topped the British bestseller list by Christmas.

questions.question: When did Japan's first bullet train line open?
questions.fact: The Tōkaidō Shinkansen began running nine days before the Tokyo Olympics opened.

questions.question: When did Yellowstone become the first national park?
questions.fact: President Grant signed it into law, and only a few hundred people visited in its first year.

questions.question: When did Krakatoa erupt, one of the most violent eruptions recorded?
questions.fact: The blast was heard 4,780 km away, on the island of Rodrigues near Mauritius.

questions.question: When did Spotify's music streaming service launch?
questions.fact: It was started as a legal alternative to music piracy.

questions.question: When did Apple sell its first computer, the Apple I?
questions.fact: It cost $666.66, and only a couple of hundred were made.
